result.document_summary: Berkeley Rent Board web page describing state and local limits on tenant screening and application fees, including the 2026 maximum screening fee and BMC chapter 13.78 requirements.
result.notes: Two records extracted: the state-law screening fee cap/refund rules (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6) as presented by the page for Berkeley, and the local BMC ch. 13.78 rules on disclosure and non-refundable fees for existing tenancies. The page gives no effective dates, so effective_date is left blank. Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 is a state law, but the page applies it to Berkeley landlords; it is recorded at the state level, with the cap stated for 2026.

rules.title: Tenant screening fee cap, receipt, refund and availability requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a screening fee up to the annual maximum ($68.96 for 2026), must provide the credit report, a receipt with itemized expenses and a refund of any unused portion, and cannot charge a fee if no unit is available. Landlords must also refund the fee to applicants not selected or follow a first-qualified-applicant policy, and must accept a reusable screening report.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to landlords of residential rental property charging screening fees to prospective tenants.
rules.interaction: Berkeley's BMC 13.78.010 requires landlords to disclose tenant screening fee rights and the maximum fee cap permitted under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b).

rules.title: Berkeley screening fee rights disclosure and ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenancies
rules.requirement: Owners charging a fee for a credit report and application processing must provide a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and the state maximum fee cap before receiving the fee. Owners may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee for renewing a tenancy or for roommate departures, additions or replacements, and chapter 13.78 overrides contrary lease terms.
rules.key_value: Disclosure of screening fee rights and fee cap; no non-refundable renewal/roommate fees
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part
rules.coverage_text: Applies to all residential rental agreements in Berkeley regardless of contrary lease language.
rules.interaction: Incorporates the maximum fee cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b) into the required disclosure.
